key_terms.rent: Rs 18,000 per month, due by the 5th
key_terms.deposit: Rs 1,00,000, refunded at vacating after deductions the landlord decides
key_terms.lock_in: 11 months for the tenant only; leaving early loses the whole deposit
key_terms.notice_period: One month for either party (but see the lock-in)
key_terms.rent_increase: Landlord can revise rent at any time

flags.title: Leaving early loses your whole deposit

quotes.text: The Lessee shall not vacate the premises before the expiry of 11 months. If the Lessee vacates earlier, the entire security deposit shall be forfeited.
Either party may terminate this agreement by giving one month's notice.

flags.explanation: You must stay the full 11 months. If you leave earlier, you lose the entire Rs 1,00,000 deposit. Clause 4 says either side can end it with one month's notice, which conflicts with this.
flags.why_it_matters: A job change or transfer could cost you Rs 1,00,000.
flags.question: Clause 4 and Clause 5 say different things. Can we remove the deposit forfeiture, or replace it with a fixed amount such as one month's rent?

flags.title: Landlord decides what to deduct

quotes.text: The deposit shall be refunded at the time of vacating after deducting such amounts as the Lessor may deem fit.

flags.explanation: The landlord can deduct any amount from your deposit without a limit or a reason.
flags.why_it_matters: You could get back much less of your deposit than you expect.
flags.question: Can deductions be limited to unpaid rent and damage beyond normal wear and tear, with bills shared?

flags.title: Deposit is over five months' rent

quotes.text: The Lessee has paid a security deposit of Rs 1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh only).

flags.explanation: Rs 1,00,000 is more than five months' rent. In Hyderabad deposits are usually one to three months' rent, and the Model Tenancy Act benchmark is two months.
flags.why_it_matters: A large amount of your money is tied up, and more is at risk if deductions are disputed.
flags.question: Can the deposit be reduced to two or three months' rent?

flags.title: Rent can go up any time

quotes.text: The rent may be revised by the Lessor from time to time.

flags.explanation: The landlord can raise the rent whenever they want, by any amount.
flags.why_it_matters: Your monthly cost could rise in the middle of the agreement.
flags.question: Can the increase be a fixed percentage, only at renewal?

flags.title: Rs 500 a day late fee, no limit

quotes.text: Rent paid after the 5th shall attract a penalty of Rs 500 per day of delay.

flags.explanation: Every day you pay late adds Rs 500. A month's delay would be about Rs 15,000, and there is no maximum.
flags.why_it_matters: A short delay, such as a salary delay, can become expensive quickly.
flags.question: Can there be a grace period of a few days and a maximum late fee?

flags.title: One month's rent for painting

quotes.text: At the time of vacating, the Lessee shall pay painting charges equal to one month's rent, irrespective of the period of stay.

flags.explanation: You pay Rs 18,000 for painting when you leave, even if you stayed only a few months. This is common in Hyderabad, but it is still worth asking about.
flags.why_it_matters: It's a fixed charge that doesn't depend on the actual cost or your length of stay.
flags.question: Can painting charges be based on the actual cost, or reduced for a shorter stay?

flags.title: Landlord can visit any time

quotes.text: The Lessor or his agents may inspect the premises at any time.

flags.explanation: The landlord or people acting for them can come in without telling you first.
flags.why_it_matters: It affects your privacy. The Model Tenancy Act benchmark is 24 hours' notice.
flags.question: Can visits need at least 24 hours' notice, except in emergencies?

missing.what: The agreement doesn't say who pays society maintenance or repairs, so you could be asked to pay for anything.
missing.question: Who pays the monthly maintenance charge and repairs, and can that be written into the agreement?

summary: Four High flags: the deposit forfeiture lock-in, open-ended deposit deductions, a large deposit, and rent that can rise at any time. Ask about these before signing.
